source.title: NASA LOLA south-pole DEM · 80 m pixels
source.frame: MOON_ME_DE421
source.projection: South polar stereographic; scale true at pole
source.nominal_coverage: 80–90 degrees south; valid pixel and complete-ray coverage checked at each site
source.citation: Barker et al. (2023), The Planetary Science Journal 4, 183
source.limitations: 80 m pixel spacing is not effective resolution. Regional slope and sampled 20 km horizon only; not rock detection or footprint-scale touchdown assessment.

terrain.method: Nearest-neighbor DEM samples, spherical curvature, surface-level observer, 20 km rays every 5 degrees. Terrain beyond 20 km, between rays, and below pixel scale is unresolved. Pixel spacing is not effective terrain resolution; slope is a regional estimate, not lander-footprint safety.

source.label: DEM effective resolution
source.limitations: Publisher effective resolution describes sampling gaps, expressed as the largest crater diameter that would not be sampled by LOLA. It is not the 80 m pixel spacing or an accuracy guarantee.
source.registration_note: Same published DE421 mean-Earth frame as the installed elevation model.

limitations: Environmental maps are context, not touchdown certification. Spatial resolution and reference-frame documentation differ between products.
Do not infer ice from permanent shadow, cold temperature or image brightness. Unknown data are never treated as zero risk.
Mapped temperatures are long-term surface statistics and are not forecasts for selected dates or spacecraft battery temperatures.
Temperature coverage is the count of populated diurnal/seasonal bins (maximum 144), not a confidence probability. Smoothing and interpolation affect derived values.
Quality layers are reported, not propagated into quantified uncertainty on visibility or landing-success probability.
Adding a layer does not overwrite terrain-screened visibility. Heating affects energy only when the user enables the explicit thermal scenario.

moon_080317.tf.distribution: Direct official NAIF download; observed SHA-256 pinned on 2026-11-11

assumptions: Planetocentric latitude; east-positive longitude; spherical lunar radius 1737.4 km.
Geometric body centers; no light time, stellar aberration, refraction, solar disk or Earth angular extent.
Coordinates, terrain and Sun/Earth vectors share the MOON_ME_DE421 frame. Older IAU_MOON example results are legacy reference geometry, not terrain-screened measurements.

The local horizon uses 20 km rays at 5-degree azimuth spacing and a surface-level observer. Distant terrain, between-ray peaks, subpixel hazards and panel/antenna mounting height are not modeled. Pixel spacing is not effective terrain resolution.
Availability uses left-endpoint samples weighted by interval duration. Transitions and blackout durations are uncertain by up to one sampling interval per boundary.
No terrain data means reference-sphere geometry only, not terrain clearance. Geometry is not power generation or guaranteed radio communication.
Sun/Earth directions use SPICE UTC-to-ET conversion; leap-second kernel is current through 2017. Future leap seconds are unknown.
Site coordinates are exploratory geographic references, not NASA-approved landing points.

Environmental maps have differing spacing and frame documentation. Temperature is long-term surface context, not mission-date battery temperature. Ice catalogue membership is regional evidence; exact-point ice remains unknown.
